story: At 9:17 on a sunny Thursday night in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at the Town Hall architectural review desk making sure his golf cart modification request is on file with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is hauling extra plastic flamingos around back so only three remain out front, while Hal reads the street bulletin board for any cart approvals before heading home. Rosa, cheerful as ever, pins up a note inviting everyone to Friday dinner at 6 PM sharp, with a friendly warning that Donna's deviled eggs contain mayo and mustard.
events: Gary (architectural review desk): Check that my cart modification request is on file with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted
Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull up the extra flamingos and carry them around back, leaving just three out front
Hal (street bulletin board): Read the postings for any cart-modification approval or other notices before heading home
Rosa (street bulletin board): Pin a note: Friday dinner at Rosa's, 6 PM sharp. Donna's deviled eggs have mayo and mustard.

gary.thought_process: I already filed my cart modification request at the review desk last tick, with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted, so that part's done. It's 9:17 PM, nobody's around, and nothing more to do at the desk until Hal reviews it. I told myself I'd check the paperwork was in order, though, and I'd rather not walk off without making sure the request actually went through and the rules are stated right. A quick look at the desk won't hurt, and then I can head home and start on the lights and wiring, keeping any sound testing well before ten.

parameters.content: Check that my cart modification request is on file with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted

donna.thought_process: Rosa's headed home to prep, and Hal's still here. Dinner's settled, my eggs are covered, and I've already said my piece about the flamingos. Tonight's flamingo job is still sitting right here, three out front and the rest out back, and I'd rather have it done before Hal's committee eyes get any ideas. Then I'll turn in early so I'm fresh for Gary's session at ten tomorrow.

parameters.content: Pull up the extra flamingos and carry them around back, leaving just three out front

hal.thought_process: Rosa already confirmed dinner at six and Donna's down to three flamingos out front, so my watchdog case against her is settled. Nothing left to ask either of them. It's past nine on a Thursday night and the street bulletin board is right here. The ledger-keeper in me wants to check whether Gary's cart paperwork or any other notice has been posted. Dinner is tomorrow, practice is at ten, and I'd like to see the facts in writing before I turn in.

parameters.content: Read the postings for any cart-modification approval or other notices before heading home

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal have both answered about allergies and what they're bringing, so there's nothing left to ask them. I already told them dinner is at six sharp and that I was heading home to prep, and I shouldn't repeat myself. Gary still needs to be reminded about Friday, and the street bulletin board is right here, so I can post a short dinner notice and a note about the mayo and mustard in Donna's eggs. Then I'll go home and start cooking.

parameters.content: Pin a note: Friday dinner at Rosa's, 6 PM sharp. Donna's deviled eggs have mayo and mustard.

matters.text: Gary Kowalski: Check that my cart modification request is on file with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
